The anchor cell (AC) is a specialized uterine cell essential for developing the vulva and connecting it to the uterus. During the L3 larval stage, it signals to underlying epidermal cells to define the vulva, then breaks through the basement membrane to link the tissues. The AC is born in L2 and arises from either the anterior (Z1.ppp) or posterior (Zn.aaa) somatic gonad lineage (Kimble and Hirsh, 1979). After invasion, the anchor cell fuses with the uterine syncytium (utse) during L4 (Newman et al., 1996). The AC is used as a model for cell invasion.

description: ADEL (Anterior Deirids E) - Sensory neurons (mechanosensory, possible pheromone-sensory). Located laterally in head, behind second bulb of pharynx. Born from AB lineage: AB plapaaaapa for ADEL. Anterior deirids with sensillar branch from dorsal process of each ADE neuron following dorsal and frequently posterior trajectory ending laterally within lateral alae in anterior third of body. Dorsal process enters nerve ring laterally and runs anteriorly through ring neuropil making small synapses to other neurons. Ventral process runs through deirid commissure to enter retrovesicular ganglion, then runs anteriorly and enters ventral ganglion where it crosses to opposite side and runs posteriorly for short distance. Use dopamine as neurotransmitter and release PDF-1 (pigment dispensing factor homolog) (Loer and Rand, 2022; Janssen et al., 2009; Sulston et al., 1975). Express receptors DOP-2 (dopamine receptor), EXP-1 (excitatory, cation-selective GABA receptor), TRP-4 (mechanosensitive TRPN channel pore-forming subunit), TYRA-3 (tyramine receptor), possibly ACR-16 (nicotinic acetylcholine receptor), and innexins CHE-7, INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-7, UNC-9 (Wormbase; Altun, 2011; Wragg et al., 2007; Feng et al., 2006; Kahn-Kirby and Bargmann, 2006; Li et al., 2006; Beg and Jorgensen, 2003; Suo et al., 2003; Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). Dopaminergic nose touch mechanoreceptors modulating locomotion behavior in response to food presence by textural mechanosensation: upon encountering bacterial lawn (or Sephadex G-200 beads) worms slow forward movement; three classes of ciliated dopaminergic neurons (CEPs, ADEs, PDEs) function redundantly in this behavior (sensing mechanosensory stimuli during crawling through bacteria and communicating with motor circuit for locomotory change) (Sawin et al., 2000). In area restricted search (ARS) motor plasticity related to food presence, CEP and PDE neurons work synergistically to mediate behavior while ADE modulates it (Hills et al., 2004). Function in anterior harsh touch sensation: laser ablation of FLP, AQR, ADE results in significant reduction of anterior harsh touch sensation, while ablation of BDU, SDQR, FLP, ADE and AQR eliminates it (Li et al., 2011). Possibly function in pheromone sensation: complete pheromone (ascaroside mixture) insensitivity of tax-2(p694) mutant suggests site of action in one or more of AFD, ASE, ADE, or BAG neurons, since tax-2(p694) mutation eliminates TAX-2 subunit expression from these but has normal expression and function in other seven neurons expressing this channel (Aillion and Thomas, 2000). Important model for understanding dopaminergic mechanosensation, food-related motor plasticity, deirid neuron function, and possible pheromone sensing. Embryonic lineage: ABplapaaaap

description: ADFL (Amphid Dual-ciliated F) - Sensory neurons (chemosensory [gustatory], oxygen-sensory). Located in lateral ganglia in the head. Born from AB lineage: AB alpppppaa . Amphid neurons with dual ciliated sensory endings exposed to external environment. Like all amphid neurons, born near the presumptive nose during embryonic development, then anchor a short projection there before cell body migrates away, stretching the dendrite out behind in a process dependent on DEX-1 or DYF-7 secreted extracellular matrix proteins (Heiman and Shaham, 2010). Dendritic process takes up FITC. Each ADF axon travels through amphid commissure to enter ventral cord, then travels anteriorly to enter nerve ring, runs dorsally within nerve ring, meets contralateral partner at dorsal midline and makes gap junction with it. Use acetylcholine and serotonin as neurotransmitters and release FLP-6, INS-1, NLP-3 neuropeptides (Pereira et al., 2015; Loer and Rand, 2022; Li and Kim, 2008; Kodama et al., 2006; Nathoo et al., 2001; Sze et al., 2000; Duerr et al., 1999). Express receptors MGL-3 (metabotropic glutamate receptor), NPR-5 (peptide receptor), OSM-9, OCR-2 (TRPV channels), SRB-6 (faint, GPCR), SRD-1 (male only, GPCR), TMC-1 (salt-sensing cation channel), and innexins CHE-7 (early larva), INX-10a, INX-19, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Wormbase; Chatzigeorgiou et al., 2013; Altun, 2011; Cohen et al., 2009; Greer et al., 2008; Tobin et al., 2002; Colbert et al., 1997; Troemel et al., 1995; Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019; Chuang et al., 2007). Only serotonergic sensory neurons in hermaphrodite worm (in males, ray sensory neurons 1B, 3B, 9B also serotonergic), coupling environmental food signals with serotonin neurotransmission (Jafari et al., 2011). Contribute to residual chemotactic response to cAMP, biotin, Cl-, Na+ after ASE ablation (Bargmann and Horvitz, 1991). C. elegans shows chemoattraction to low NaCl mediated by four amphid neuron pairs (ADF, ASE, ASG, ASI) with ASE most important; under hypoxic conditions, additional latent circuit involving ADF and ASG activates for processing chemosensory information (Pocock and Hobert, 2010). Salt response is plastic, balancing attraction and avoidance involving ASE, ASI, ASH, ADF and perhaps ADL neurons (Hukema et al., 2006). Control dauer entry: ADF, ASI, ASG inhibit dauer entry while ASJ, ASK promote it (Kim et al., 2009; Ouellett et al., 2008; Schackwitz et al., 1996; Bargmann and Horvitz, 1991). Function as part of oxygen-sensing network (also includes URX, AQR, PQR, SDQ, ALN, PLN, ADL, ASH) by promoting hyperoxia avoidance; ADF stimulates aerotaxis in absence of food by producing serotonin (Chang et al., 2006). Modulate neuromuscular junction (NMJ) neurotransmission: endogenous serotonin from ADF stimulates acetylcholine synaptic transmission at NMJs, whereas serotonin from NSM/RIH/AIM neurons inhibits the stimulatory serotonin inputs; exogenous serotonin inhibits aldicarb-induced paralysis but not levamisole-induced paralysis, suggesting serotonin signaling inhibits ACh release by motor neurons (Govorunova et al., 2010). Important model for understanding serotonergic modulation, oxygen sensing, chemotaxis plasticity, and neuromodulation of motor circuits. Embryonic lineage: ABalpppppa

description: ADLL (Amphid Dual-ciliated L) - Sensory neurons (chemosensory, odorsensory, pheromone-sensory, nociceptive). Located in lateral ganglia in the head. Born from AB lineage: AB alppppaad. Amphid neurons with dual (AdL) ciliated sensory endings. Like all amphid neurons, born near the presumptive nose during embryonic development, then anchor a short projection there before cell body migrates away, stretching the dendrite out behind in a process dependent on DEX-1 or DYF-7 secreted extracellular matrix proteins (Heiman and Shaham, 2010). Dendritic process takes up FITC. Each axon enters nerve ring from lateral side directly, running both dorsally and ventrally within ring; dorsal branch meets contralateral partner at midline making gap junction. Sister cells undergo apoptosis. Use glutamate as neurotransmitter and release FLP-4, FLP-21, NLP-7, NLP-8, NLP-10 neuropeptides (Li and Kim, 2008; Rogers et al., 2003; Nathoo et al., 2001). Express receptors GCY-21 (transmembrane guanylyl cyclase), OSM-9, OCR-1, OCR-2 (TRPV channels), SER-6 (octopamine receptor), SRB-6, SRE-1, SRH-132, SRH-220, SRI-51, SRO-1 (GPCRs), TMC-1 (salt-sensing cation channel), and innexins CHE-7, INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-7, INX-10a, INX-14, INX-18a, INX-19, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Wormbase; Chatzigeorgiou et al., 2013; Mills et al., 2012; Altun, 2011; Tobin et al., 2002; de Bono et al., 2002; Colbert et al., 1997; Troemel et al., 1995; Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019; Chuang et al., 2007; Liu et al., 2006). Play minor role in avoidance from chemical repellents evident when ASH missing, with ASH being major sensor (de Bono and Maricq, 2005; Hilliard et al., 2002; Sambongi et al., 1999; Bargmann et al., 1990). Mediate avoidance from heavy metals (Cd2+, Cu2+), odors (octanol), high osmotic strength, SDS (Sambongi et al., 1999; Troemel et al., 1995). Balance NaCl response with ASE, ASI, ASH, ADF (Hukema et al., 2006). With ASH, mediate social feeding behavior in response to repulsive cues (high O2): ablation abolishes social feeding transforming social to solitary feeders; OCR-2, OSM-9, ODR-4 in ADL/ASH promote high O2 avoidance facilitating aggregation, transmitting aversive environmental information to circuits controlling aggregation, rapid locomotion, food bordering (Rogers et al., 2006; de Bono et al., 2002). Sense pheromones (ascaroside mixtures) involved in dauer entry and adult behaviors (Jang et al., 2012; Lockery, 2009; Macosko et al., 2009). Important model for nociception and social behavior regulation.

description: AFDL (Amphid Finger-like D Left) - The AFD neurons are ciliated amphid sensory neurons (thermosensory and CO2-sensory). The AFD cell bodies are located near the anterior border of the lateral ganglia.  The AFDs have anterior dendrites that end near the amphid pore. The distal tip of the AFD dendrites have a single cilia surrounded by dozens of microvilli leading to a finger-like appearance.  The AFD cilia and microvilli are embedded within the distal ending of the amphid sheath glia. The number of microvilli expand during the dauer stage (Albert and Riddle, 1983). The axons of AFD extend ventrally towards and into the ventral cord via the amphid commissure. The axons then enter the nerve ring and run dorsally around the outer posterior edge where their main synaptic output is to the AIY interneurons. AFDL is born from AB lineage (AB alpppapav) at approximately 275 minutes after the first cellular cleavage at 20° C and is sister to RMDL. The AFD cell bodies are born near the presumptive nose during embryonic development, then anchor a short projection there before the cell body migrates away, stretching the dendrite out behind (Heiman and Shaham, 2010).  Embryonic lineage: ABalpppapa
function: Use glutamate as neurotransmitter and release FLP-6, NLP-7, NLP-21, possibly PDF-1 neuropeptides (Barrios et al., 2012; Ohnishi et al., 2011; Loer and Rand, 2022; Li and Kim, 2008; Rogers et al., 2003; Nathoo et al., 2001). Express receptors GCY-8, GCY-18, GCY-23 (transmembrane guanylyl cyclases redundantly producing cGMP in AFD; gcy-23, gcy-8, gcy-18 triple mutants show cryophilic or athermotactic phenotype), GCY-29 (transmembrane guanylyl cyclase), TMC-1 (salt-sensing cation channel), and innexins CHE-7, INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-7, INX-10a, INX-19, UNC-7 (Wormbase; Chatzigeorgiou et al., 2013; Ortiz et al., 2006; Inada et al., 2006; Yu et al., 1997; Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019; Chuang et al., 2007; Liu et al., 2006). Main thermosensors in C. elegans; laser ablation of AFD pair makes most animals athermotactic (Ma and Shen, 2012; Beverly et al., 2011; Kuhara et al., 2008; Satterlee et al., 2004; Mori and Ohshima, 1995). After cultivation at uniform temperature (Tc) with food, animals preferentially migrate to Tc on thermal gradient and move isothermally; animals sense and memorize Tc by AFD (major thermosensory), AWC, ASI neurons (Beverly et al., 2011; Kuhara et al., 2008; Biron et al., 2008). Memory is plastic and resets upon different temperature cultivation (Hedgecock and Russell, 1975). Animals track isotherms by suppressing turns once serendipitously aligned along isotherm (Luo et al., 2006). Increase reversal and turn frequency detecting temperature rise, moving back down gradient toward Tc (negative thermotaxis). Respond to thermal stimuli above Tc with continuous, graded calcium signals due to Ca2+ influx via cGMP-dependent TAX-2/TAX-4 cation channels; AFD, AWC, ASI may act in concert increasing turning rate at higher temperatures (Biron et al., 2008). Thermal information transmitted by AFD and AWC to AIY interneurons for processing, with AIY transmitting to AIZ and RIA for further processing. Activation by warming above Tc induces reversal by inhibiting AIY (AFD ablation suppresses spontaneous reversals in AIY-dependent manner; AIY ablation increases spontaneous reversals) (de Bono and Maricq, 2005; Tsalik and Hobert, 2003). GPCR SRTX-1 required in both AFD and AWC for normal isothermal tracking (Liu et al., 2012). In addition to viable range temperature sensing (~15-25°C), participate in noxious temperature thermonociception (~35-38°C) inducing temperature avoidance response with reflex-like escape reaction along with FLP (head) and PHC (tail) neurons; avoidance requires TAX-2, TAX-4 cell autonomously in AFD and TRPV channels (OCR-2/OSM-9) in FLP and PHC (Liu et al., 2012). For ambient temperature, cGMP production through GCY-23, GCY-8, GCY-18; for noxious heat, mainly through GCY-12. Noxious temperature avoidance via AFD involves AIB interneuron. Laser ablations cause hyporeversal phenotype (Tsalik and Hobert, 2003). Primary CO2 sensors along with BAG and ASE (oxygen-sensing neurons AQR, PQR, URX weakly CO2 responsive); AFD and BAG together stimulate turning when CO2 rises and inhibit turning when CO2 falls (Bretscher et al., 2011). May be involved in social feeding since disruption of tax-2 expression in AFD, AQR, ASE, BAG disrupts social feeding (Coates and de Bono, 2002). Premier model for studying thermosensation, most extensively studied thermosensory neuron, essential for understanding temperature memory and thermotaxis algorithms.

description: AIBL (Amphid I Neuron Class B) - Interneurons. Located in lateral ganglia in the head. Born from AB lineage: AB plaapappa. Amphid interneurons with process traveling through amphid commissure to enter ventral cord, then traveling anteriorly to enter nerve ring, running dorsally with brief anterior turn at midline, then round the nerve ring, reentering ventral cord on opposite side and ending within ventral ganglion. Use betaine and glutamate as neurotransmitters and release FLP-20 neuropeptide (Wang et al., 2024; Pereira et al., 2015; Li and Kim, 2008). Express receptors GLR-1, GLR-2 (glutamate-activated cation channels), possibly GLR-5 (kainate-type glutamate receptor), possibly GGR-1 (GABA-A/glycine receptor-like), possibly MGL-2 (metabotropic glutamate receptor), and innexins INX-1, INX-2, INX-6 (dauer only), INX-7, INX-10a, INX-18a, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Wormbase; Fujiwara et al., 1996; Maricq et al., 1995; Brockie et al., 2001; Kang and Avery, 2009; Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). One of four first-layer amphid interneuron pairs (AIA, AIB, AIY, AIZ) receiving and processing synaptic output from amphid sensory neurons. AIA pair sums inputs from chemosensory neurons before passing information to AIB which synapses onto motor neurons, with AIA-AIB connections likely inhibitory (Wakayabashi et al., 2004). Function in locomotion with AIB not affecting turning rates while AIA and AIY inhibit turns (Garrity et al., 2010; Wakayabashi et al., 2004). Process information within AWC-AIB-AIY circuit controlling food- and odor-evoked behaviors: after food removal, animals initiate local search behavior (reversals and omega turns) followed by dispersal ~30 min later; local search triggered by AWC olfactory neurons, ASK gustatory neurons, and AIB interneurons, while dispersal promoted by ASI gustatory neurons and AIY interneurons (Gray et al., 2005). AWC neurons activated by odor removal activate AIB through AMPA-type glutamate receptors while inhibiting AIY through glutamate-gated chloride channels, with opposite regulation generating coordinated behavioral response (Chalasani et al., 2007). Regulate lifespan and starvation response (starvation induces heat-shock resistance, oxidative stress resistance, lifespan extension): amino acids (leu, gln, ala, val, ile) act as anti-hunger signaling molecules activating AIY and inhibiting AIB by modulating MGL-1 and MGL-2 metabotropic glutamate receptors; AIY inhibits starvation response while AIB activates it (Shen et al., 2010; Kang and Avery, 2009). Important model for understanding sensory integration, first-layer processing, and how interneurons combine multiple sensory modalities for context-dependent behavior. Embryonic lineage: ABplaapapp

description: AIYL (Amphid I Neuron Class Y) - Interneurons. Located in ventral ganglion in the head. Born from AB lineage: AB plpapaaap. Amphid interneurons with process entering nerve ring from ventral side, running dorsally within nerve ring, meeting contralateral partner at dorsal midline and making gap junction with it. Use acetylcholine as neurotransmitter and release FLP-1 and FLP-18 neuropeptides (Li and Kim, 2008; Rogers et al., 2003; Altun-Gultekin et al., 2001). Express receptors ACR-14 (nicotinic AChR alpha subunit), C50F7.1 (tachykinin receptor-like), CKR-2 (cholecystokinin receptor-like), GAR-2 (muscarinic AChR), and innexins INX-1, INX-2, INX-7, INX-10a, INX-14, INX-18a, INX-18b, INX-19, UNC-9 (Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019; Chuang et al., 2007). One of four first-layer amphid interneuron pairs (AIA, AIB, AIY, AIZ) receiving and processing synaptic output from amphid sensory neurons. Postsynaptic to several olfactory and gustatory sensory neurons (ASE, ASI, AWA, AWC, AFD), playing integrative role processing multiple sensory information streams with key role in behavioral plasticity when starvation paired with thermal or chemical cues (de Bono and Maricq, 2005; Ishihara et al., 2002). Function in thermotaxis: ablation makes animals cryophilic and impairs isothermal tracking (Mori and Ohshima, 1995). Thermal information from AFD, AWC, ASI processed in thermotaxis core interneurons AIY, AIZ, RIA and likely AIA, AIB (Ma and Shen, 2012; Sasakura and Mori, 2012; Ardiel and Rankin, 2011; Beverly et al., 2011). In two-drive thermotaxis model, AIY activation drives warm-seeking (thermophilic) movement, AIZ activation drives cold-seeking (cryophilic), with counterbalancing through RIA executing motor output (Ohnishi et al., 2011; Kuhara et al., 2008). Major postsynaptic partner of AWC and AFD: AWC glutamatergic signals stimulate AIY inducing warmer temperature migration (Ohnishi et al., 2011); AFD transmits both inhibitory and stimulatory signals to AIY with calcium threshold in AFD acting as switch for opposing signals directing opposite behaviors (Kuhara et al., 2011). AFD glutamatergic signals inhibit AIY through GLC-3 glutamate-gated chloride channel driving colder temperature migration, with AFD/AIY synapse evolved for reliable transmission of scaled-down temperature signal enabling AIY to monitor and integrate temperature with other sensory inputs (Narayan et al., 2011). Suppress turns and reversals enhancing smooth forward movements and dispersal: ablation increases reversals and turns, disrupts dispersal behavior, shortens forward movements (Gray et al., 2005; Wakayabashi et al., 2004; Tsalik and Hobert, 2003). Process information within AWC-AIB-AIY circuit: AWC activated by odor removal activates AIB through AMPA receptors while inhibiting AIY through glutamate-gated chloride channels; odor presentation relieves inhibition activating AIY, with opposite regulation generating coordinated response (Chalasani et al., 2007). Regulate lifespan and starvation response: amino acid signals activate AIY (inhibiting starvation response) and inhibit AIB (activating it) by modulating MGL-1 and MGL-2 metabotropic glutamate receptors (Shen et al., 2010; Kang and Avery, 2009). Most extensively studied chemosensory interneuron, essential for understanding chemotaxis algorithms, thermotaxis, and premier example of how interneuron connectivity implements behavioral algorithms. Embryonic lineage: ABplpapaaa

description: AIZL (Amphid I Neuron Class Z) - Interneurons. Located in lateral ganglia in the head. Born from AB lineage: AB plapaaapav for AIZL. Ring interneurons with process of each AIZ neuron traveling through amphid commissure to enter ventral cord, then traveling anteriorly to enter nerve ring, running dorsally within nerve ring, meeting contralateral partner at dorsal midline and making gap junction with it. Use glutamate as neurotransmitter and release FLP-22 neuropeptide (Loer and Rand, 2022; Li and Kim, 2008; Lee et al., 1999). Express receptors SER-2 (tyramine receptor, two separate splice variants) and innexins INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-7, INX-10a, INX-14, INX-19, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Altun, 2011; Tsalik et al., 2003; Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). One of four first-layer amphid interneuron pairs (AIA, AIB, AIY, AIZ) receiving and processing synaptic output from amphid sensory neurons toward behavioral response. Along with second-layer RIA and RIB interneurons, receive heavy input from first layer AIA, AIB, AIY interneurons and send outputs to RIA and RIB. Synapse directly onto SMB head motor neurons. Function in thermotaxis: along with AIY and RIA, are thermotaxis core interneurons (Sasakura and Mori, 2012). Laser ablation makes animals thermophilic. Thermal information from AFD, AWC, ASI processed in downstream interneurons AIY, AIZ, RIA and likely AIA, AIB. In original two-drive thermotaxis model, AIY activation drives warm-seeking (thermophilic) movement, AIZ activation drives cold-seeking (cryophilic) movement, with counterbalancing between AIY and AIZ signals possibly through RIA executing motor output in response to thermal signals. However, evidence suggests thermophilic drive below cultivation temperature (Tc) does not exist and thermotaxis regulation involves more complex circuit: around Tc animals track isothermally on gradient, above Tc display negative thermotaxis by regulating turning frequency and run duration; thermosensory signals from AFD, AWC, ASI converge on AIB in negative thermotaxis, while AIY/AIZ/RIA network may function mainly in isothermal tracking (Ma and Shen, 2012; Sasakura and Mori, 2012; Ardiel and Rankin, 2011; Beverly et al., 2011; Ohnishi et al., 2011; Kuhara et al., 2008; Ryu and Samuel, 2002; Mori and Ohshima, 1995). During associative learning between temperature and feeding state, starvation (conditioning factor) downregulates AIZ activity through calcineurin/TAX-6 (calcium-activated phosphatase), leading to Tc avoidance (Kuhara and Mori, 2006). Function in locomotion: laser ablation, like AIB and AWC, causes decreased reversals and large increases in forward movement duration; since AIY and AIZ ablations cause opposite behavioral phenotypes, AIY synapses onto AIZ may be inhibitory, or signals from AIY to AIZ could be processed in downstream neuron such as RIA (Iino and Yoshida, 2009; de Bono and Maricq, 2005; Tsalik and Hobert, 2003). Function in chemotaxis: laser ablation causes defects in weathervane (slow turning by biased head swing) and pirouette (bout of sharp turns generated by frequent reversals followed by omega turns) responses, leading to impaired chemotaxis (Iino and Yoshida, 2009). Important model for understanding thermotaxis, cold-seeking behavior, and integration of thermal information with locomotor output. Embryonic lineage: ABplapaaapa

description: ALML (Anterior Lateral Microtubule Cells) - The ALMs are mechanosensory neurons. The cell bodies are located laterally in mid-body after migrating during embryonic development from their birthplace at the anterior edge of the intestine.  ALML is among the six non-ciliated touch receptor neurons (TRN) that extend long, 15-protofilament microtubule (MT)-filled neurites in close apposition to the hypodermis and cuticle. The ALM processes extend anteriorly past the nerve ring and lie between the seam cells and the subdorsal body wall muscle, often embedded with the lateral hypodermis. ALML is born from AB lineage: AB arppaappa.
function: The ALMs detect gentle touch that mediate backwards movement in response to mechanical stimuli. Mechanical force applied to ALM is transmitted to the membrane via MTs, causing membrane stretch that activates mechanosensory channel-opening rather than direct MT-channel gating (Cueva et al., 2007). Surrounded by specialized extracellular matrix called "mantle" around neurites. Spontaneous neural activity endogenously decreases during larval lethargus (Schwarz et al., 2011). Express MEC-3, MEC-4, and MEC-10 mechanosensory channel subunits. Founding members of the mechanosensory neuron class in Chalfie's Nobel Prize-winning work (2008). Essential model for mechanotransduction, extensively used with mec-4::GFP and mec-7::GFP markers in behavioral studies of touch response and habituation.

description: AMshL (Amphid sheath left) is one of two bilateral glial sheath cells that wrap the ciliated endings of amphid sensory neurons. The AMsh cell bodies migrate from just posterior of the pharyngeal terminal bulb in L1 to adjacent to the dorsal and anterior edge of the pharyngeal terminal bulb (Sulston, 1977). The AMsh cells have an anterior process that ends near the amphid pore and connects with the AMso cells to create a channel for amphid channel neurons. Amphid sensory neuron endings of AFD, AWA, AWB, and AWC are embedded with the expanded AMsh ending. AMshL is born within the AB embryonic lineage (ABplaapaapp) at approximately 300 minutes after the first cell cleave at 20° C and is the sister cell to URBL.

description: AQR (Amphid QR neuron) - Sensory neuron (oxygen- and minor CO2-sensory). Located in head on right side near posterior bulb of pharynx. Born postembryonically from QR.ap lineage. Postembryonically born neuron with rudimentary cilium. AQR and its ciliated dendrite are directly exposed to pseudocoelomic body fluid. Axonal process projects into ring. Uses glutamate as neurotransmitter (Pereira et al., 2015). Expresses receptors GCY-25 (transmembrane guanylyl cyclase), GCY-32, GCY-34, GCY-35 (binds molecular oxygen mediating oxygen sensation, heterodimerizes with GCY-36), GCY-36, GCY-37 (soluble guanylyl cyclases), NPR-1 (peptide receptor), and innexins CHE-7, INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-7, INX-10a, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Bhattacharya et al., 2019). Functions in aerotaxis along with PQR, URX, AUA, regulating social feeding (aggregation on bacterial lawn) and bordering (accumulation on thickest part of bacterial lawn) behaviors; suppressing activity of AQR, PQR, URX inhibits social feeding (Coates and de Bono, 2002). Function as sensors of environmental oxygen quantitatively regulating social feeding (Gray et al., 2004). Animals carrying npr-1 (215F) low-activity allele or lacking npr-1 function dwell (slow down) on food in low ambient O2 and roam/aggregate (at food borders) in high ambient O2; O2 drops increase GCY-35/GCY-36 heterodimeric soluble guanylyl cyclase activity, rising cGMP opens TAX-2/TAX-4 cGMP-gated ion channel in AQR, PQR, URX leading to depolarization and strong roaming behavior suppression when food present (in npr-1 mutants these neurons hyperactive) (Cheung et al., 2005). Suppress innate immunity via NPR-1, regulating both PMK-1-dependent and PMK-1-independent immune responses (Styer et al., 2008). Since URX, AQR, PQR are exposed to pseudocoelomic fluid, hypothesized to communicate neuroendocrine signals to nonneural tissues involved in innate immunity defense responses. Weak CO2-sensors contributing to CO2 avoidance (main CO2 sensors are AFD, BAG, ASE) (Bretscher et al., 2011). Important model for understanding oxygen sensing, social behavior regulation, and neuroendocrine control of immunity.

description: AS1-AS11 (AS-type Motor Neurons 1-11) - Motor neurons. Located in body (ventral nerve cord). Born postembryonically from lineages: P1.apa (AS1), P2.apa (AS2), P3.apa (AS3), P4.apa (AS4), P5.apa (AS5), P6.apa (AS6), P7.apa (AS7), P8.apa (AS8), P9.apa (AS9), P10.apa (AS10), P11.apa (AS11). Ventral cord motor neurons innervating dorsal muscles with no ventral counterpart, similar to VA neurons but receiving additional synaptic input from AVB. Unlike AS1-10, commissure of AS11 originates from posterior process. All AS commissures to dorsal cord occur on right side of body. Hermaphrodites and males exhibit some differences in AS connectivity; in males, AS11 cell body lies posterior to male-specific CP9 neuron defining anterior boundary of male preanal ganglion, thus AS11 considered part of preanal ganglion rather than ventral nerve cord in males. Use acetylcholine as neurotransmitter and release NLP-21 neuropeptide (Loer and Rand, 2022; Duerr et al., 2008; von Stetina et al., 2007; Rand and Nonet, 1997). Express receptors ACR-14 (nicotinic AChR non-alpha subunit), ACR-15 (nicotinic AChR alpha subunit), LGC-46 (ligand-gated ion channel), UNC-63 (levamisole-sensitive nicotinic acetylcholine receptor alpha subunit), and innexins INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-3, UNC-7, INX-10a, INX-14, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Wormbase; Altun, 2011; von Stetina et al., 2007; Fox et al., 2005; Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019; Starich et al., 2009). Coordinate body wave propagation during locomotion (Tolstenkov et al., 2018). Make chemical synapses to other motor neurons (DA, DD, VD), receive chemical synapses from AVA, AVB, AVD, AVE command interneurons, and form gap junctions with DA, VA, AVA. description: ASEL (Amphid Single-ciliated E) - Sensory neurons (chemosensory [gustatory], CO2-sensory). Located in lateral ganglia of head. Born from AB lineage: AB alppppppaa. Amphid neurons with single ciliated endings. Like all amphid neurons, born near the presumptive nose during embryonic development, then anchor a short projection there before cell body migrates away, stretching the dendrite out behind in a process dependent on DEX-1 or DYF-7 secreted extracellular matrix proteins (Heiman and Shaham, 2010). Axon projects into ring via amphid commissure from ventral ganglion, making diverse synaptic connections in ring neuropil. Although left-right anatomical homologs, exhibit marked asymmetries in gene expression and function (Cochella and Hobert, 2012). Use glutamate as neurotransmitter and release extensive neuropeptide repertoire including FLP-4 (ASEL only), FLP-6, FLP-13, FLP-20 (ASEL only), FLP-25, INS-1, INS-22, INS-26, INS-32 (ASEL only), NLP-3, NLP-5 (ASER only), NLP-7, NLP-14 (Pereira et al., 2015; Takayama et al., 2010; Li and Kim, 2008; Etchberger et al., 2007; Johnston et al., 2005; Kim and Li, 2004; Rogers et al., 2003; Nathoo et al., 2001; Pierce et al., 2001). Express asymmetric receptors: ASEL expresses GCY-6, GCY-7, GCY-14, GCY-20 (transmembrane guanylyl cyclases for Na+ sensing), while ASER expresses GCY-1, GCY-3, GCY-4, GCY-5, GCY-22 (for Cl-/K+ sensing), plus bilateral GCY-29, and additional receptors DEL-3, DEL-4 (DEG/ENaC channels), DAF-2 (possibly ASER), DOP-3, DOP-5 (dopamine receptors), MGL-3 (metabotropic glutamate receptor), NPR-1, NPR-5, NPR-15 (peptide receptors), OSM-9 (TRPV), SRAB-14, SRD-33, SRG-30, SRX-76 (GPCRs), TMC-1 (salt-sensing cation channel), TRPA-2, TRP-2 (ASER only), TYRA-2 (tyramine receptor), and innexins CHE-7, INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-7, INX-10a, INX-14, UNC-7 (dauer only), UNC-9 (Wormbase; Chatzigeorgiou et al., 2013; Mills et al., 2012; Altun, 2011; Takayama et al., 2010; Etchberger et al., 2007; Ortiz et al., 2006; Tomioka et al., 2006; Coates and de Bono, 2002; Colbert et al., 1997; Yu et al., 1997; Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). Most important neurons for chemotaxis to water-soluble attractants including Na+, Cl-, cAMP, biotin, lysine; simultaneous ablation of all amphid and phasmid neurons except ASE spares chemotaxis (Bargmann, 2006). ASEL primarily sensitive to Na+ (ON-cell activated by NaCl increases), ASER primarily sensitive to Cl- and K+ (OFF-cell tonically active at baseline, deactivated by NaCl increases), generating opposite intracellular Ca2+ transients; ASEL activation inhibits reversals and lengthens forward locomotion, ASER activation promotes reversals and turns, implementing biased random walk toward chemoattractants (Appelby, 2012; Suzuki et al., 2008; Suzuki et al., 2004; Pierce-Shimomura et al., 2001; Bargmann and Horvitz, 1991). Play minor role in avoidance from chemical repellents including Cd2+ and Cu2+ when ASH neurons absent (Hilliard et al., 2002; Sambongi et al., 1999; Bargmann et al., 1990). Function in adaptive food-leaving behavior, promoting departure from depleting food patches via cGMP pathway involving DAF-2 insulin receptor in ASER and INS-1-dependent feedback from AIA to ASER, switching salt attraction to repulsion during food withdrawal (Milward et al., 2011; Tomioka et al., 2006). Primary CO2 sensors along with AFD and BAG; both ASEL and ASER activated when CO2 rises, unlike their asymmetric NaCl response (Bretscher et al., 2011). Premier model for studying left-right asymmetry in nervous system, essential for understanding gustatory sensation, ion sensing mechanisms, and guanylyl cyclase signaling.

description: AVM (Anterior Ventral Microtubule Cell) - Sensory neuron (mechanosensory) detecting gentle touch to the anterior body, postembryonically born touch receptor. Expresses PDFR-1 (pigment dispersing factor receptor) (Barrios et al., 2012). Core member of the six touch receptor neurons essential for mechanosensory behavior studies and featured in Chalfie's Nobel Prize-winning mechanotransduction research.

description: AWCL (Amphid Wing Cells C Left) - The AWC neurons are ciliated amphid sensory neurons (odorsensory, photosensory, electrosensory and thermosensory). The cell bodies of the AWCs are located near the ventral edge of the lateral ganglia. The AWCs have anterior dendritic processes that end near the amphid pore. The distal endings of the AWC dendrites are ciliated with sheet-like sensory endings embedded within the amphid sheath glia. These sheet-like wings expand during the dauer stage in response to amphid sheath cell remodeling (Albert and Riddle, 1983; Procko et al., 2011). The axons of the AWCs extend ventrally via the amphid commissure and then towards and into the nerve ring where its main  synaptic outputs include AIB, AIY, and AIA. AWCL is born from AB lineage (AB plpaaaaap) at approximately 300 minutes after first cleavage at 20° C and is sister to SAAVL. The AWC cell bodies are born near the presumptive nose during embryonic development, then anchor a short projection there before the cell body migrates away, stretching the dendrite out behind (Heiman and Shaham, 2010).
function: Display functional asymmetry where one AWC stochastically expresses chemoreceptor STR-2 (AWC^ON state), creating left-right asymmetry (Troemel et al., 1999). Use glutamate as neurotransmitter (AWC-AIA synapse is inhibitory glutamatergic, modulated by NLP-1/NPR-11 signaling) and release NLP-1 neuropeptide (Chalasani et al., 2010; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013). Express receptors OSM-9 (TRPV channel), DAF-11 (guanylyl cyclase), STR-2 (GPCR, asymmetrically expressed), and innexins CHE-7, INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-7, INX-10a, INX-14, INX-18a, INX-19, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Birnby et al., 2000; Troemel et al., 1999; Colbert et al., 1997; Chuang et al., 2007; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). Critical for chemotaxis to volatile odorants (benzaldehyde, butanone, isoamylalcohol, 2,3 pentanedione, 2,4,5 trimethylthiazole). Function as odor-OFF neurons activated by odor removal and inhibited by continued odor presence. Trigger local search behavior after food removal, synapsing onto AIB (activating through AMPA receptors, enhancing turning) and AIY (inhibiting through glutamate-gated chloride channels, suppressing turning), with NLP-1 required for food-evoked behaviors and odor adaptation (Chalasani et al., 2010; Gray et al., 2005; L'Etoile and Bargmann, 2000; Bargmann et al., 1993). Serve as thermosensors along with AFD and ASI for temperature cultivation (Tc) memory and thermotaxis: Ca2+ increases via ODR-1 cGMP production and TAX-4 channel activation at temperatures above Tc, exhibiting stochastic temperature-evoked Ca2+ changes with stimulus-correlated temporal kinetics, becoming more active as temperatures diverge from Tc (Beverly et al., 2011; Kuhara et al., 2008; Biron et al., 2008). GPCR SRTX-1 required in both AFD and AWC for isothermal tracking (Liu et al., 2012). Contribute to electrosensory navigation toward negative pole (Gabel et al., 2007). One of three core sensory neurons (AWA, AWC, ASK) required for male sexual attraction (White and Jorgensen, 2012). Most extensively studied chemosensory neuron and paradigm for understanding olfactory coding, stochastic left-right asymmetry, and sensory adaptation.

function: Display functional asymmetry where one AWC stochastically expresses chemoreceptor STR-2 (AWC^ON state), creating left-right asymmetry (Troemel et al., 1999). Use glutamate as neurotransmitter (AWC-AIA synapse is inhibitory glutamatergic, modulated by NLP-1/NPR-11 signaling) and release NLP-1 neuropeptide (Chalasani et al., 2010; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013). Express receptors OSM-9 (TRPV channel), DAF-11 (guanylyl cyclase), STR-2 (GPCR, asymmetrically expressed), and innexins CHE-7, INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-7, INX-10a, INX-14, INX-18a, INX-19, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Birnby et al., 2000; Troemel et al., 1999; Colbert et al., 1997; Chuang et al., 2007; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). Critical for chemotaxis to volatile odorants (benzaldehyde, butanone, isoamylalcohol, 2,3 pentanedione, 2,4,5 trimethylthiazole). Function as odor-OFF neurons activated by odor removal and inhibited by continued odor presence. Trigger local search behavior after food removal, synapsing onto AIB (activating through AMPA receptors, enhancing turning) and AIY (inhibiting through glutamate-gated chloride channels, suppressing turning), with NLP-1 required for food-evoked behaviors and odor adaptation (Chalasani et al., 2010; Gray et al., 2005; L'Etoile and Bargmann, 2000; Bargmann et al., 1993). Serve as thermosensors along with AFD and ASI for temperature cultivation (Tc) memory and thermotaxis: Ca2+ increases via ODR-1 cGMP production and TAX-4 channel activation at temperatures above Tc, exhibiting stochastic temperature-evoked Ca2+ changes with stimulus-correlated temporal kinetics, becoming more active as temperatures diverge from Tc (Beverly et al., 2011; Kuhara et al., 2008; Biron et al., 2008). GPCR SRTX-1 required in both AFD and AWC for isothermal tracking (Liu et al., 2012). Contribute to electrosensory navigation toward negative pole (Gabel et al., 2007). One of three core sensory neurons (AWA, AWC, ASK) required for male sexual attraction (White and Jorgensen, 2012). Most extensively studied chemosensory neuron and paradigm for understanding olfactory coding, stochastic left-right asymmetry, and sensory adaptation.

description: CEPDL (Cephalic Neurons) - Sensory neurons (mechanosensory). Located in head with dorsal CEP cell bodies just posterior of nerve ring, ventral CEP cell bodies just anterior of nerve ring. Born from AB lineage: AB plaaaaappa for CEPDL. Neurons of cephalic sensilla with dendrite extending to nose tip within corresponding labial nerve. CEPD neurons directly exposed to pseudocoelomic body fluid. Function in mechanosensation in head: deflection of single cilium by pressure application produces ion currents in CEP neuron consistent with mechanosensory function (Kang et al., 2010). Three classes of dopaminergic neurons (CEP, ADE, PDE) function redundantly to sense mechanosensory stimulus from bacteria and mediate motor circuit to control "basal slowing response": when well-fed C. elegans hermaphrodites washed clean of bacteria then reintroduced to bacterial lawn, they move more slowly than when transferred to environment without bacteria (Sawin et al., 2000). Important model for understanding dopaminergic mechanosensation, food-related motor plasticity, and redundant sensory pathways.

description: DB1-DB7 (Dorsal B Motor Neurons 1-7) - Ventral cord motor neurons, proprioceptive neurons. Located in body (ventral nerve cord). Born from AB lineage (AB plpaaaapp or AB prpaaaapp for DB1/3, AB arappappa for DB2, AB prpaaaapp or AB plpaaaapp for DB3/1, AB prpappapp for DB4, AB plpapappp for DB5, AB plppaappp for DB6, AB prppaappp for DB7). Ventral cord "dorsal B" motor neurons receiving extensive input from PVC and innervating dorsal muscles and VD neurons. Use acetylcholine as neurotransmitter (Duerr et al., 2008; Rand and Nonet, 1997). Express receptors ACR-14 (nicotinic AChR non-alpha subunit), possibly PDFR-1 (pigment dispersing factor receptor in DB2), and innexins INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-3, INX-14, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Barrios et al., 2012; Fox et al., 2005; Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). Function in forward locomotion: VD neurons activated during forward movement (Haspel et al., 2010); ablation of five of seven DB neurons causes defects in larval forward movement (Chalfie et al., 1985). Function in proprioception involving propagation of rhythmic activities along body during forward locomotion: ventral and dorsal bending of anterior body region directly activates VB and DB motor neurons (Wen et al., 2012); gap junctions between neighbors and overlapping process segments propagate bending signal from anterior to posterior, with mechanosensitive-proprioceptive receptors likely localized near anterior of processes. Make chemical synapses to other motor neurons (AS, DD, VD), receive chemical synapses from DVA, PVC, PVR, and form gap junctions with DB, VB, AVB (Haspel & Donovan, 2011). Representative of B-class motor neurons essential for forward locomotion. Important for understanding proprioception, rhythmic motor pattern generation, and mechanosensitive feedback during locomotion.

description: DD1-DD6 (Dorsal D Motor Neurons 1-6) - Motor neurons. Located in body (ventral nerve cord). Born from AB lineage (AB plppappap for DD1, AB prppappap for DD2, AB plppapppa for DD3, AB prppapppa for DD4, AB plppapppp for DD5, AB prppapppp for DD6). GABAergic inhibitory ventral cord motor neurons receiving dyadic synapses from excitatory ventral cord motor neurons along with body wall muscles. Initial synaptic pattern is presynaptic and inhibitory to ventral body wall muscles while being postsynaptic to neurons activating dorsal body wall muscles. During late L1, after VD motor neuron birth, DD neurons change synaptic pattern such that dorsal branches become presynaptic and inhibitory to dorsal body wall muscles while ventral branches become postsynaptic to excitatory neurons synapsing on ventral body wall muscles (White et al., 1978; Walthall et al., 1993). Hermaphrodites and males exhibit some differences in DD connectivity. Use GABA as neurotransmitter (McIntire et al., 1993; Rand and Nonet, 1997). Express receptor ACR-14 (nicotinic AChR non-alpha subunit) and innexins INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-3, INX-10, INX-14, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Fox et al., 2005; Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). Function in sinusoidal body movement-locomotion: ablation causes uncoordinated movement in larvae (Chalfie et al., 1985); optogenetic activation reduces ventral body wall muscle activity in L1 and lesser reduction of dorsal body wall activity (Lu et al., 2022). Make chemical synapses to other motor neurons (VD), receive chemical synapses from RID and VC1-3, and form gap junctions with DD and VD. Important model for understanding GABAergic inhibitory motor control, synaptic remodeling during development, and reciprocal inhibition in locomotion circuits.

description: DVA (Dorsal V neuron A) - Interneuron, stretch sensitive sensory neuron. Located in dorsorectal ganglion. Born from AB lineage (AB prppppapp). Monopolar ring interneuron with cell body located in dorsorectal ganglion, sending process the length of ventral cord and entering into right side of nerve ring. Uses acetylcholine as neurotransmitter (note: DVA is cholinergic while DVC is not) (Pereira et al., 2015; Duerr et al., 2008). Expresses receptors possibly GGR-3 (GABA-A/glycine receptor-like), GLR-4, GLR-5 (glutamate receptor subunits), NMR-1 (NMDA receptor subunit), SER-2 (tyramine receptor splice variant), SER-4 (serotonin receptor, variably expressed - neuron can be DVC instead), TRP-4 (mechanosensitive TRPN channel), and innexins INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-3, INX-7, INX-10, INX-13, INX-14, INX-17, INX-18, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Li et al., 2006; Tsalik et al., 2003; Brockie et al., 2001; Fujiwara et al., 1996; Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). Function in mechanosensory integration: PVD and DVA neurons are presynaptic to both forward and backing interneurons, providing input to both anterior and posterior touch circuits; animals lacking these neurons respond to tap stimulus with diminished forward accelerations and reversals, suggesting these neurons maintain overall activity of touch circuit (Wicks et al., 1996; Driscoll and Kaplan, 1997; Goodman, 2007). Function in proprioception: DVA represents stretch receptor neuron regulating sensory-motor integration during C. elegans locomotion; trp-4 (mechanosensitive TRPN channel homologue) acts as stretch-sensitive proprioceptor in DVA; DVA both positively and negatively modulates locomotion, providing unique mechanism whereby single neuron can fine-tune motor activity (Li et al., 2006). Important model for understanding proprioception, stretch sensation, mechanosensory integration, and dual excitatory/inhibitory modulation of motor circuits.

description: FLPL (Anterior Lateral Neurons) - Sensory neurons (polymodal nociceptive for mechanosensation and thermosensation). Located in the head. Born from AB lineage: AB plapaaapad. Not part of a sensillum. Multidendritic neurons with arborization structure very similar to PVD neurons, topologically covering head and neck while PVD covers the rest of the body (Hall and Treinin, 2011; Hall and Altun, 2008). Primary dendrites have ciliated endings in head which are not open to outside, wrapping around a branch of the lateral ILso cell just below the region where the socket cell surrounds the IL neurons. Use glutamate as neurotransmitter and release FLP-4 and FLP-21 neuropeptides (Loer and Rand, 2022; Li and Kim, 2008; Lee et al., 1999). Express mechanosensory channels DEL-1, MEC-10, UNC-8 (DEG/ENaC subunits), TRPV channel OSM-9, receptors DEG-3, DES-2 (nAChR subunits), GLR-4 (glutamate receptor), and PDFR-1, along with innexins CHE-7, INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-7, INX-10a (dauer only), INX-14, INX-18a, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Wormbase; Altun, 2011; Brockie et al., 2001; Treinin et al., 1998; Colbert et al., 1997; Tavernarakis et al., 1997). Mediate harsh nose touch response accounting for 29% of normal response (Goodman, 2006; Kaplan and Driscoll, 1997). Also respond to gentle nose touch activating escape behavior, with OLQ and CEP neurons facilitating responses via RIH interneuron integration (Chatzigeorgiou and Schafer, 2011). Sense noxious temperatures (~35-38°C) inducing thermonociceptive escape reaction requiring TRPV channels (OCR-2/OSM-9), working with AFD and PHC neurons (Liu et al., 2012). Essential model for studying polymodal nociception and thermonociception in anterior body region.

description: IL1DL (Inner Labial 1) - Polymodal neurons (sensory neuron [mechanosensory], motor neuron, interneuron). Located in head. Born from AB lineage: AB alapappaaa for IL1DL. Neurons of inner labial sensilla with ciliated endings with striated rootlets, synapsing directly onto muscle cells. IL1 dendrite ending does not protrude through hole in socket cell to outside. Use glutamate as neurotransmitter (Pereira et al., 2015). Express receptors DEG-3 (nicotinic acetylcholine receptor alpha subunit), MEC-6 (degenerin/epithelial Na+ channel complex component interacting with MEC-4), TRPA-1 (transient receptor potential ion channel), and innexins CHE-7, INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-10a, INX-12, INX-14, INX-18, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Wormbase; Kindt et al., 2007; Chelur et al., 2002; Treinin and Chalfie, 1995; Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). Mediate head-withdrawal reflex: when worms touched on dorsal or ventral nose sides with eyelash during forward movement, they interrupt normal foraging pattern and undergo aversive head-withdrawal reflex; simple reflex mediated by two mechanosensory neuron classes (OLQ and IL1) and their synaptic targets (RMD motor neurons), with killing any of these cells alone or in combination diminishing reflex (Goodman, 2006; Kaplan and Driscoll, 1997; Hart et al., 1995). IL1, OLQ, and RMD also regulate spontaneous foraging movements; laser-operated animals lacking IL1 and OLQ forage abnormally slowly and make exaggerated dorsal and ventral nose turns (Hart et al., 1995). TRPA-1 function in IL1 and OLQ and GLR-1 function in RMD neurons facilitate both foraging rate and head withdrawal (Kindt et al., 2007). Important model for understanding polymodal neuron function, mechanosensory processing in head, and simple reflex circuits.

description: IL2DL (Inner Labial 2 Dorsal Left) is one of six sensory neuron with a ciliated dendritic ending that protrude through the inner-labial sensilla pore. The IL2 neuron cell bodies are located in the anterior ganglion. During all non-dauer stages, the IL2 neurons have a single anteriorly directed dendrite that ends in a cilia exposed to the environment.  The distal tip of the IL2s is slightly longer than the adjacent IL1s. Unlike the IL1 neurons,  IL2 dendrites lack rootlets. During dauer, the dorsal and ventral IL2 neurons exhibit dendritic branching and the extension of additional primary dendrites that are resorbed during recovery from dauer (Schroeder et al., 2013). The IL2 neurons extend a single posteriorly directed axon that passes the outer edge of the nerve ring and then turns anteriorly into the ring. The primary synaptic output of the dorsal and ventral IL2s are to the RIPs, IL1s, and RMEs.  IL2DL is born from AB lineage (AB alapappap) at approximately 300 minutes, at 20 C, after the first cell cleavage. The sister cell of IL2DL divides an additional time to form IL1DL and a cell that undergoes cell death. The IL2 neurons can stain with DiI/Ca Acetate, DiO, Di4ANEPPS and RH421 (Burket et al., 2006; Mille and Shakes, 1995).
function: Sensory neurons (polymodal sensory?, chemosensory?, mechanosensory?). Use acetylcholine and unknown monoamine as neurotransmitters (not glutamatergic as earlier reports suggested) (Wang et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2014; Loer and Rand, 2022; Duerr et al., 2008; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013; Lee et al., 1999). Express receptors DES-2 (nicotinic acetylcholine receptor alpha subunit), NPR-1 (neuropeptide Y receptor-like, in IL2L/R), and innexins CHE-7 (dauer only), INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-10a, INX-11, INX-14, INX-18 (IL2L/R only), UNC-7, UNC-9 (Coates and de Bono, 2002; Treinin et al., 2001; Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). Regulate nictation, a dispersal behavior seen in dauer larvae; intact IL2 cilia and cholinergic transmission in IL2 neurons required for this function (Lee et al., 2012). Targeted activation of IL2 neurons in non-dauers does not induce nictation, possibly since IL2 neurons undergo significant structural change at dauer stage which may be required for behavior control (Albert and Riddle, 1983). Important model for understanding neuroplasticity, dauer-specific structural remodeling, and stage-specific behaviors.

Neurons of inner labial sensilla with ciliated endings without rootlets. IL2 dendrite ending protrudes through hole in socket cell to outside, suggesting chemosensory function. Stain with DiI/Ca Acetate, DiO, Di4ANEPPS and RH421 (Burket et al., 2006; Mille and Shakes, 1995). Although six IL2 neurons have similar gross structure and express many same genes, lateral IL2s display different neuronal connectivity and morphology than quadrant (dorsal & ventral) ones (Wang et al., 2010; MoW). Display neuroplasticity and stage-specific remodeling: dorsal and ventral IL2s undergo significant dendrite arborization and axon remodeling during dauer development (much less striking in lateral IL2s); when dauer larvae return to favorable conditions, dendritic arbors retract leaving remnant branches in postdauer L4 and adult animals (Schroeder et al., 2013). Use acetylcholine and unknown monoamine as neurotransmitters (not glutamatergic as earlier reports suggested) (Wang et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2014; Loer and Rand, 2022; Duerr et al., 2008; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013; Lee et al., 1999). Express receptors DES-2 (nicotinic acetylcholine receptor alpha subunit), NPR-1 (neuropeptide Y receptor-like, in IL2L/R), and innexins CHE-7 (dauer only), INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-10a, INX-11, INX-14, INX-18 (IL2L/R only), UNC-7, UNC-9 (Coates and de Bono, 2002; Treinin et al., 2001; Altun et al., 2009; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). Regulate nictation, a dispersal behavior seen in dauer larvae; intact IL2 cilia and cholinergic transmission in IL2 neurons required for this function (Lee et al., 2012). Targeted activation of IL2 neurons in non-dauers does not induce nictation, possibly since IL2 neurons undergo significant structural change at dauer stage which may be required for behavior control (Albert and Riddle, 1983). Important model for understanding neuroplasticity, dauer-specific structural remodeling, and stage-specific behaviors.

description: OLQDL (Outer Labial Quadrant) - Polymodal neurons (sensory neuron - mechanosensory, interneuron). Located in head. Born from AB lineage: AB alapapapaa for OLQDL. Neurons of outer labial lateral sensilla with dendrites having ciliated endings with striated rootlets, terminating embedded within cuticle of nose. Use glutamate as neurotransmitter (Lee et al., 1999). Express receptors OCR-4, OSM-9 (TRPV channels), NPR-1 (peptide receptor), TRPA-1 (transient receptor potential ion channel), and innexins INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-10a, INX-14, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Wormbase; Altun, 2011; Kindt et al., 2007; Coates and de Bono, 2002; Tobin et al., 2002; Colbert et al., 1997; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). IL1, OLQ, and RMD regulate spontaneous foraging movements: in presence of food, C. elegans makes rapid nose oscillations termed 'foraging' as they explore environment; laser-operated animals lacking IL1 and OLQ forage abnormally slowly and make exaggerated dorsal and ventral nose turns (Hart et al., 1995; Kaplan and Driscoll, 1997; Goodman, 2006). Mediate head-withdrawal reflex: when worms touched on ventral or dorsal nose side during forward movement, respond with aversive head movement away from stimulus; simple reflex mediated by two mechanosensory neuron classes (OLQ and IL1) and their synaptic targets (RMD motor neurons), with killing any of these cells alone or in combination diminishing reflex (Kaplan and Driscoll, 1997; Kindt et al., 2007). TRPA-1 function in IL1 and OLQ and GLR-1 function in RMD neurons facilitate both foraging rate and head withdrawal (Kindt et al., 2007). Important model for understanding nose mechanosensation, foraging behavior, and simple reflex circuits.

description: PLML (Posterior Lateral Microtubule Left) - The PLMs are mechanosensory neurons. The cell bodies are located in the lumbar ganglia. is among the six non-ciliated touch receptor neurons (TRN) that extend long, 15-protofilament microtubule (MT)-filled neurites in close apposition to the hypodermis and cuticle. The PLMs extends a short posterior process towards the tail tip and a long anterior process along the ventral edge of the lateral hypodermal ridge. Near the vulva, the PLML anterior process sends a branch towards the ventral nerve cord, but does not enter the cord. PLML is born from the AB lineage: AB plapappppaa.
function: Along with AVM and ALM, PLM neurons sense gentle (low threshold) mechanical stimulus and provide input to command interneurons (PVC, AVB, AVD, AVA) via synaptic connections and gap junctions. In the escape response circuit, posterior touch cells PLML/R form gap junctions with forward movement interneuron PVC (agonist) but provide synaptic input to backward movement interneurons AVA and AVD (Goodman, 2006; Chalfie et al., 1985; Kaplan and Driscoll, 1997). Use glutamate as neurotransmitter (Lee et al., 1999). Express mechanosensory channel complex components MEC-2 (stomatin-like protein), MEC-4 (DEG/ENaC subunit), MEC-6 (degenerin complex protein), and MEC-9 (extracellular attachment point), along with receptors DEG-3, DES-2 (nAChR subunits), DOP-1 (dopamine receptor), GLR-8 (glutamate receptor), and PDFR-1 (Wormbase; Barrios et al., 2012; Sanyal et al., 2004; Chelur et al., 2002). Involved in memory formation for habituation to tap response with both 12-hr and 48-hr memory retention, requiring FLP-20-dependent increase of synaptic vesicles in PLM terminals and CREB/GLR-1 in postsynaptic AVA/AVD interneurons (Timbers and Rankin, 2011; Li et al., 2013). Most extensively studied mechanosensory neuron and standard model for touch transduction research.

description: PQR (P neuron QR) - Sensory neuron (oxygen- and minor CO2-sensory). Located in left lumbar ganglia. Born postembryonically from left Q neuroblast (QL.ap lineage), migrates posteriorly to position near phasmid neurons in left lumbar ganglion. Single neuron with basal body, directly exposed to pseudocoelomic body fluid (internal environment). Anterior process projects into preanal ganglion, usually ending just posterior to vulva (can be slightly shorter or longer). Posterior process ensheathed by PHso2L cell. Uses glutamate as neurotransmitter (Pereira et al., 2015). Expresses receptors GCY-32 (guanylyl cyclase), GCY-35 (guanylyl cyclase binding molecular oxygen mediating oxygen sensation), NPR-1 (neuropeptide Y receptor-like), PDFR-1 (pigment dispersing factor receptor), and innexins CHE-7, INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-7, INX-10a, INX-11, INX-18a, UNC-9 (Barrios et al., 2012; Gray et al., 2004; Coates and de Bono, 2002; Yu et al., 1997; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). Functions in aerotaxis along with AQR, URX, AUA, regulating social feeding (aggregation on bacterial lawn) and bordering (accumulation on thickest bacterial lawn part) behaviors; suppressing activity of AQR, PQR, URX inhibits social feeding (Coates and de Bono, 2002). Function as sensors of environmental oxygen quantitatively regulating social feeding (Gray et al., 2004). Animals carrying npr-1 (215F) allele or lacking npr-1 function dwell (slow down) in low ambient O2 and roam (disperse) or aggregate in high ambient O2; O2 drops increase GCY-35/GCY-36 heterodimeric soluble guanylyl cyclase activity, rising cGMP opens TAX-2/TAX-4 cGMP-gated ion channel in AQR, PQR, URX causing depolarization and strong roaming behavior suppression with food present (in npr-1 mutants these neurons hyperactive) (Cheung et al., 2005). Suppress innate immunity via NPR-1 regulating both PMK-1-dependent and -independent immune responses (Styer et al., 2008); exposure to pseudocoelomic fluid suggests communication of neuroendocrine signals to nonneural tissues for innate immunity defense responses. Weak CO2-sensors contributing to CO2 avoidance (main sensors AFD, BAG, ASE) (Bretscher et al., 2011). Part of neuronal circuit functioning in mate-searching behavior of males (Barrios et al., 2012). Important model for understanding oxygen sensing, social behavior, and tail-based sensory processing.

PVC processes enter nerve cord via lumbar commissures and run on right side of hypodermal ridge in nerve cord. description: PVDL (Polymodal Nociceptors) - Sensory neurons (polymodal nociceptive for mechanosensation and thermosensation). Located in tail, lumbar ganglion. Born postembryonically from V lineage: V5L.paapa. Feature extensive branching pattern that develops progressively: in early larval stages show three major processes (anteriorly directed, posteriorly directed, ventrally directed) with short extensions; starting from L2, branching pattern elaborates extensively through growth and retraction, forming well-ordered, repeating menorah-like units by L4 (Oren-Suissa et al., 2010). Quaternary branches are 30-60 nm in diameter. Unlike touch receptor neurons, branches have no prominent cytoskeletons and are not linked to body wall through specialized mantle of extracellular matrix (Hall and Treinin, 2011). Final menorah array is non-overlapping and regularly spaced, topologically covering most of the body except neck and head (Hall and Treinin, 2011; Oren-Suissa et al., 2010; Smith et al., 2010; Hall and Altun, 2008). In adult males, produce extra branches entering tail rays potentially involved in mating behavior (Iosilevskii et al., 2025). Use glutamate as neurotransmitter and release NLP-11 neuropeptide (Nathoo et al., 2001; Lee et al., 1999). Express mechanosensory channels DEGT-1 and MEC-10 (colocalize on primary and tertiary branches), MEC-6, MEC-9, TRPA-1 (cold sensing), OSM-9 (TRPV), receptors DEG-3, DES-2 (nAChR subunits), GLR-4, SER-2 (tyramine receptor), and innexins INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-5, INX-7, INX-10a, INX-12, INX-14, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Wormbase; Xiao et al., 2013; Altun, 2011; Kindt et al., 2007; Tsalik et al., 2003). Respond to harsh touch as stretch-sensing mechanosensors (requiring MEC-10 and DEGT-1) and cold temperatures causing cold hyperalgesia (requiring TRPA-1 channel, MEC-10/DEGT-1-independent), demonstrating polymodal nociception involves parallel sensory transduction channels (Chatzigeorgiou et al., 2010; Way and Chalfie, 1989). Harsh mechanical stimulus stretches tertiary processes by displacing quaternary branches, transmitting pulling force that opens DEG/ENaC channels in primary and tertiary neurites (Hall and Treinin, 2011). Premier model for studying dendritic arbor development, self-avoidance, tiling, nociception, and parallel sensory transduction mechanisms.

description: RIAL (Ring Interneuron A) - Interneurons. Located in head. Born from AB lineage: AB alapaapaa for RIAL. Receive synaptic inputs from AIY and AIZ interneurons and densely innervate head motor neurons SMD and RMD. Use glutamate as neurotransmitter (Pereira et al., 2015). Express receptor SER-1 (serotonin receptor) and innexins INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-7, INX-10a, INX-14, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Dernovici et al., 2007; Carnell et al., 2005; Bhattacharya et al., 2019). Classified as "second layer" interneurons in integration of information from outside world and inner state of animal leading to behavioral response. Function in thermotaxis: along with AIY and AIZ, are thermotaxis core interneurons; RIA mutation impairing function or laser ablation causes athermotactic or cryophilic behavior, with killing RIA having no effect on chemotaxis (Iino and Yoshida, 2009; Tanizawa et al., 2006; Mori and Ohshima, 1995). In original two-drive (thermophilic vs cryophilic) thermotaxis model, RIA integrates signals processed in thermotaxis neural circuit and emits outputs to downstream neurons (Mori and Ohshima, 1995; Tanizawa et al., 2006). Multiple signals including EAT-4-dependent glutamatergic neurotransmission from RIA communicate processed information to downstream neurons generating ultimate thermotactic outputs (Ohnishi et al., 2011). Although downstream neurons of RIA as main circuit components unclear, RIA heavily connected presynaptically to SMD or RMD head motor neurons regulating turning behavior, suggesting SMD and RMD control turn frequency and run duration depending on thermal information transmitted by RIA (Ohnishi et al., 2011; Zariwala et al., 2003; White et al., 1986; Gray et al., 2005). Function in locomotion: killing RIA slightly decreases reversals during local search and dispersal (Gray et al., 2005). Important model for understanding second-layer interneuron function, thermotaxis circuit integration, and glutamatergic control of motor output.

description: RIML (Ring Interneuron M) - Motor neurons, interneurons. Located in lateral ganglia of head. Born from AB lineage: AB plppaapap for RIML. RIM neurons send processes into nerve ring via amphid commissures, innervating muscles in head via neuromuscular junctions in nerve ring. Use betaine, glutamate, and tyramine as neurotransmitters (Wang et al., 2024; Loer and Rand, 2022; Alkema et al., 2005). Express innexins CHE-7, INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-7, INX-10a, INX-14, INX-18a, INX-19, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Bhattacharya et al., 2019; Altun et al., 2009). Classified as "second layer" interneurons in integration of information from outside world and inner state of animal leading to behavioral response. Function in locomotion circuit with RIM neurons modulating reversals by two opposing roles: photostimulation of RIM induces worm reversal requiring AVA/AVD/AVE neurons (Guo et al., 2009); RIM and AVA activity correlated through gap junctions while RIM inhibits AVB (Alkema et al., 2005; Pirri et al., 2009). Anterior touch activates AVA which activates RIM; tyramine release from RIM activates tyramine-gated chloride channel LGC-55 on AVB forward locomotion command neurons, neurons of head movement circuit (RMD and SMD), and neck muscles; LGC-55 activation causes hyperpolarization of neck muscles and AVB neurons inducing suppression of head movements and sustained backward locomotion (reversal) in response to anterior touch (Pirri and Alkema, 2011). However, optogenetic ablation of RIM increases reversal frequency, suggesting RIM inhibits initiation of reversals during locomotion (Piggott et al., 2011; Husson et al., 2013). Suppression of RIM activity can trigger reversals independently of command interneurons for backward locomotion (AVA/AVD/AVE) through disinhibition circuit involving AIB upstream of RIM, considered parallel pathway for reversal initiation. Important model for understanding dual excitatory/inhibitory roles, tyraminergic neurotransmission, and parallel pathways for behavioral control.

description: RIVL (Ring Interneuron/motor neuron V) - Polymodal neurons (interneuron, motor neuron). Located in head with cell bodies situated subdorsally in lateral ganglia. Born from AB lineage: AB plpaapaaa for RIVL. Use acetylcholine as neurotransmitter (Pereira et al., 2015). Function in locomotion: after food removal, animals initiate local search behavior consisting of reversals and deep omega-shaped turns, followed by dispersal ~30 min later as reversals and turns are suppressed; local search triggered by AWC olfactory neurons, ASK gustatory neurons, and AIB interneurons, while dispersal promoted by ASI gustatory neurons and AIY interneurons (Gray et al., 2005). Downstream of AIB and AIY, motor neurons define specific aspects of reversal and turn frequency, amplitude, and directionality: SMD motor neurons define steep amplitude of omega turns, RIV motor neurons specify ventral bias of turns that follow reversal, and SMB motor neurons set amplitude of sinusoidal movement. Important model for understanding dual interneuron/motor neuron function, turn directionality control, and hierarchical organization of locomotor behaviors.

description: RMDDL (Ring Motor Neuron D) - Motor neurons. Located in head. Born from AB lineage: AB alpapapaa for RMDDL. Ring motor neurons innervating muscles in head via neuromuscular junctions in nerve ring. Use acetylcholine as neurotransmitter (not glutamatergic as earlier reports suggested) (Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013; Ohnishi et al., 2011; Loer and Rand, 2022; Duerr et al., 2008). Express receptor GLR-1 (AMPA-type ionotropic glutamate receptor) and innexins INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-7, INX-10a, INX-14, INX-19, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Maricq et al., 1995; Bhattacharya et al., 2019; Altun et al., 2009). IL1, OLQ, and RMD regulate spontaneous foraging movements: in presence of food, C. elegans makes rapid nose oscillations termed 'foraging' as they explore environment; laser-operated animals lacking IL1 and OLQ forage abnormally slowly and make exaggerated dorsal and ventral nose turns (Goodman, 2006; Kaplan and Driscoll, 1997; Hart et al., 1995). Mediate head-withdrawal reflex: when worms touched on ventral or dorsal nose side during forward movement, respond with aversive head movement away from stimulus; simple reflex mediated by two mechanosensory neuron classes (OLQ and IL1) and their synaptic targets (RMD motor neurons), with killing any of these cells alone or in combination diminishing reflex (Kaplan and Driscoll, 1997; Kindt et al., 2007). TRPA-1 function in IL1 and OLQ and GLR-1 function in RMD neurons facilitate both foraging rate and head withdrawal (Kindt et al., 2007). Important model for understanding head motor control, simple reflex circuits, foraging behavior, and mechanosensory-motor integration.

Ring motor neurons innervating muscles in head via neuromuscular junctions in nerve ring. Use acetylcholine as neurotransmitter (not glutamatergic as earlier reports suggested) (Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013; Ohnishi et al., 2011; Loer and Rand, 2022; Duerr et al., 2008). Express receptor GLR-1 (AMPA-type ionotropic glutamate receptor) and innexins INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-7, INX-10a, INX-14, INX-19, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Maricq et al., 1995; Bhattacharya et al., 2019; Altun et al., 2009). IL1, OLQ, and RMD regulate spontaneous foraging movements: in presence of food, C. elegans makes rapid nose oscillations termed 'foraging' as they explore environment; laser-operated animals lacking IL1 and OLQ forage abnormally slowly and make exaggerated dorsal and ventral nose turns (Goodman, 2006; Kaplan and Driscoll, 1997; Hart et al., 1995). Mediate head-withdrawal reflex: when worms touched on ventral or dorsal nose side during forward movement, respond with aversive head movement away from stimulus; simple reflex mediated by two mechanosensory neuron classes (OLQ and IL1) and their synaptic targets (RMD motor neurons), with killing any of these cells alone or in combination diminishing reflex (Kaplan and Driscoll, 1997; Kindt et al., 2007). TRPA-1 function in IL1 and OLQ and GLR-1 function in RMD neurons facilitate both foraging rate and head withdrawal (Kindt et al., 2007). Important model for understanding head motor control, simple reflex circuits, foraging behavior, and mechanosensory-motor integration.

description: SMBDL (Submedial Motor Neuron B) - Motor neurons. Located in head. Born from AB lineage: AB alpapapapp for SMBDL. Innervate muscles in head via neuromuscular junctions in nerve ring and send processes posteriorly down sublateral cords. Use acetylcholine as neurotransmitter (Loer and Rand, 2022; Duerr et al., 2008; Rand and Nonet, 1997). Express innexins INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-10a, INX-14 (dauer only), UNC-7, UNC-9 (Bhattacharya et al., 2019; Altun et al., 2009). Function in locomotion: after food removal, animals initiate local search behavior consisting of reversals and deep omega-shaped turns, followed by dispersal ~30 min later as reversals and turns are suppressed; local search triggered by AWC olfactory neurons, ASK gustatory neurons, and AIB interneurons, while dispersal promoted by ASI gustatory neurons and AIY interneurons (Gray et al., 2005). Downstream of AIB and AIY, motor neurons define specific aspects of reversal and turn frequency, amplitude, and directionality: SMD motor neurons define steep amplitude of omega turns, RIV motor neurons specify ventral bias of turns following reversal, and SMB motor neurons set amplitude of sinusoidal movement. Important model for understanding head motor control, sinusoidal movement amplitude regulation, and hierarchical organization of locomotor behaviors.

description: URXL (UR neurons X) - Sensory neurons (oxygen and minor CO2), also ring interneurons. Located in head. Born from AB lineage: AB plaaaaappp. Nonciliated dendritic endings in nose associated with CEPD in embryo, terminating in flat, membranous and branched processes around ILso endings (Doroquez et al., 2014). Unlike retrograde extension of amphid dendrites during embryonic development, URX dendrite likely extends from stationary cell body with OL glia possibly as adhesive guide (McLachlan and Heiman, 2013). Like AQR and PQR, directly exposed to pseudocoelomic fluid, proposed to monitor contents of this fluid. Use acetylcholine and betaine as neurotransmitters and release FLP-8, FLP-10, FLP-11, FLP-19 neuropeptides (Wang et al., 2024; Pereira et al., 2015; Li and Kim, 2008). Express receptors GCY-1, GCY-25 (transmembrane guanylyl cyclases), GCY-32, GCY-34, GCY-35 (binds molecular oxygen mediating oxygen sensation, heterodimerizes with GCY-36), GCY-36, GCY-37 (soluble guanylyl cyclases), NPR-1 (peptide receptor), PDFR-1 (pigment dispersing factor receptor), SRA-10 (GPCR), and innexins CHE-7, INX-1a, INX-1b, INX-2, INX-10a, INX-14, INX-18a, INX-18b, UNC-7, UNC-9 (Wormbase; Barrios et al., 2012; Cheung et al., 2004; Gray et al., 2004; Troemel et al., 1995; Bhattacharya et al., 2019; Altun et al., 2009). Function in aerotaxis along with AQR, PQR, AUA, regulating social feeding (aggregation on bacterial lawn) and bordering (accumulation on thickest bacterial lawn part) behaviors. C. elegans in O2 gradient shows strong preference for ~5-10% (intermediate) O2, avoiding hypoxia (<7%) and hyperoxia (21%), navigating gradients through O2-induced locomotion speed, reversal and turning changes (Cheung et al., 2005; Gray et al., 2004). Intermediate O2 preference allows oxidative metabolism while avoiding oxidative stress (Lee and Atkinson, 1977), promotes aggregation behavior as aggregating worms locally deplete O2 to preferred levels (Gray et al., 2004; Rogers et al., 2006). O2 rise leaving group induces reversal and turning; O2 fall entering group suppresses reversal, turning, rapid locomotion, allowing staying with group. Soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC)-expressing oxygen-sensing neurons (URX, BAG, AQR, PQR, SDQ, BDU, ALN, PLN) mediate ambient O2 responses (Zimmer et al., 2009). URX most important for aggregation (Coates and de Bono, 2002), redundant with other sGC-expressing neurons for aerotactic behavior in O2 gradient (Chang et al., 2006). description: VA1 (Ventral A Motor Neurons) - Motor neurons. Located in body (ventral nerve cord). Born postembryonically from lineages: W.pa. Important for understanding coordinated dorsal-ventral muscle activation, motor pattern generation, and how bilateral motor coordination produces sinusoidal locomotion.

Born postembryonically from lineages: P1.aaap (VB1), W.aap (VB2), P2.aaap (VB3), P3.aaap (VB4), P4.aaap (VB5), P5.aaap (VB6), P6.aaap (VB7), P7.aaap (VB8), P8.aaap (VB9), P9.aaap (VB10), P10.aaap (VB11). Function in locomotion and proprioception involving propagation of rhythmic activities along body during forward locomotion: ventral and dorsal bending of anterior body region directly activates VB and DB motor neurons (Wen et al., 2012); gap junctions between neighbors and overlapping process segments propagate bending signal from anterior to posterior, with mechanosensitive-proprioceptive receptors likely localized near anterior of processes. Make chemical synapses to other motor neurons (DD, VA, VD), receive chemical synapses from PVC, and form gap junctions with VB, DB, AVB. Represent B-class motor neurons essential for forward locomotion. Important for understanding proprioception, mechanosensitive feedback during locomotion, postembryonic motor neuron development, and rhythmic motor pattern generation.

Born postembryonically from lineages: P1.aaap (VB1), W.aap (VB2), P2.aaap (VB3), P3.aaap (VB4), P4.aaap (VB5), P5.aaap (VB6), P6.aaap (VB7), P7.aaap (VB8), P8.aaap (VB9), P9.aaap (VB10), P10.aaap (VB11). Ventral cord motor neurons with connectivity of VB1, VB4, and VB7 differing slightly from remaining VBs (Haspel and Donovan, 2011). Use acetylcholine and betaine as neurotransmitters (Wang et al., 2024; Loer and Rand, 2022; Duerr et al., 2008; Rand and Nonet, 1997). Express innexins INX-3, INX-12, UNC-9 (Altun et al., 2009). Function in locomotion and proprioception involving propagation of rhythmic activities along body during forward locomotion: ventral and dorsal bending of anterior body region directly activates VB and DB motor neurons (Wen et al., 2012); gap junctions between neighbors and overlapping process segments propagate bending signal from anterior to posterior, with mechanosensitive-proprioceptive receptors likely localized near anterior of processes. Make chemical synapses to other motor neurons (DD, VA, VD), receive chemical synapses from PVC, and form gap junctions with VB, DB, AVB. Represent B-class motor neurons essential for forward locomotion. Important for understanding proprioception, mechanosensitive feedback during locomotion, postembryonic motor neuron development, and rhythmic motor pattern generation.

description: VD1-VD13 (Ventral D Motor Neurons 1-13) - Motor neurons. Located in body (ventral nerve cord). Important for understanding GABAergic inhibition in locomotor circuits, postembryonic motor neuron development, and reciprocal inhibition coordinating dorsal-ventral muscle activity.
